title: Finite normalized-component cover of a proper scheme of dimension at most one
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] admit finite enumerations $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ of the one-dimensional components and $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ of the zero-dimensional components, each given its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. These schemes are integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and proper over $k$; each $P_j$ has a singleton underlying space, open and closed in $X$, and the component images cover $X$. For each $i$, the normalization $\nu_i:\widetilde C_i\to C_i$ [def-sc-normalization] is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and $\widetilde C_i$ is integral and proper over $k$ of dimension one. Let $Z=(\coprod_{i=1}^t\widetilde C_i)\amalg(\coprod_{j=1}^rP_j)$ be the scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and let $f:Z\to X$ be induced by the normalization maps followed by the component inclusions and by the inclusions of the $P_j$. Then $f$ is finite and surjective and $Z$ is proper over $k$. Both index sets are empty exactly when $X$ is empty, in which case $Z$ is empty as well.

source.place: Tag 0B5Y, lemma-ampleness-in-terms-of-degrees-components, proof: finite surjective component cover (details omitted); replace each curve component by its normalization using Tag 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic.

proof.text: A field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, generated respectively by the empty set and $1$, so it is Noetherian. The one-point affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is therefore locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Properness includes finite type; apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to obtain that $X$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] and [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], its components form a finite covering family. Each component is nonempty and closed; every chain of irreducible closed subsets in it is also a chain in $X$. Thus its dimension is either $0$ or $1$. Partition and enumerate the finite family as $P_1,\ldots,P_r$ and $C_1,\ldots,C_t$.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Properties Tag 0BA8, lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components; Topology Tag 004W, lemma-irreducible. These supply the finiteness omitted in Varieties Tag 0B5Y.

proof.text: For each component $D$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] supplies its reduced induced closed subscheme and inclusion $i_D:D\hookrightarrow X$, with underlying space precisely the component. It is nonempty and irreducible, so reducedness makes it integral by the equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The inclusion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and $D$ is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c). In particular its structure map is of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ also makes $D$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01J3 and 01J4, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme and definition-reduced-induced-scheme; Morphisms Tags 035C and 01W5, lemma-closed-immersion-finite and lemma-closed-immersion-proper; Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] to each $P_j$. A nonempty irreducible discrete space has exactly one point: two points would separate it into a singleton and its complement, both closed and proper. Write $|P_j|=\{p_j\}$. If another component contained $p_j$, it would contain $|P_j|$, contradicting maximality of $P_j$ as an irreducible subset. Since the components cover $X$, the complement of $\{p_j\}$ is exactly the union of the other components. This is a finite union of closed subsets. Thus $\{p_j\}$ is open, and it is closed because it is a component.

source.place: Tag 0AAX, lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0; the singleton and open-and-closed assertions then follow from component maximality and the finite covering family (Topology Tag 004W).

proof.text: For each $C_i$, the finite-type integral normalization theorem [lem-sc-normalization-exists] applies by Step 2. It gives that $\nu_i$ is finite and surjective, that $\widetilde C_i$ is proper over $k$, and that $\dim\widetilde C_i=\dim C_i=1$. To verify integrality as well, apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] with $X=C_i$, its unique generic point $x$ from [lem-sc-scheme-sober], and the degree-one extension $K=\kappa(x)$. Here $C_i$ is separated over $k$, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], and $K$ is its function field by [def-sc-function-field]. The normalization in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ described in that node is exactly [def-sc-normalization]: both are the relative spectrum of the integral closure of $\mathcal O_{C_i}$ in the constant function field. Its conclusion (a) therefore gives that $\widetilde C_i$ is integral. No perfectness or algebraic closure of $k$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0BXR, lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic; Morphisms Tag 035L, lemma-normal-normalization, applied to the generic field; normalization dimension and properness as in the cited existing normalization theorem.

proof.text: Form $Z$ and its map $f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each map $\widetilde C_i\to X$ is the composite of the finite map $\nu_i$ and the finite component inclusion, hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]; each $P_j\to X$ is finite by Step 2. Induct on the number $t+r$ of summands: the empty map $\varnothing\to X$ is finite, since over any affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}0\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the zero algebra is a finite $A$-module. Adding a summand preserves finiteness by the binary statement [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct]. The iterated binary coproduct and the displayed $Z$ agree by their universal property, with their maps to $X$. Hence $f$ is finite, including for zero summands.

source.place: Tags 01WK and 0CYI, lemma-composition-finite and lemma-finite-union-finite; the latter is stated for any finite number of summands, here derived from the cited binary node by induction. Schemes Tags 01JB and 01JC supply the coproduct.

proof.text: Every point of $X$ is on a component by Step 1. On a curve component it lifts along the surjection $\nu_i$ of Step 4; on a point component it is already in the image of $P_j$. The corresponding coprojection into $Z$ then supplies a preimage under $f$, so $f$ is surjective. Since $f$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] makes it proper; compose with the proper structure map of $X$ using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] to obtain that $Z$ is proper over $k$. Finally, all components are nonempty and their images cover $X$: the two index sets are empty if and only if $X$ is empty. When they are empty, the union-of-images assertion for scheme coproducts says $Z=\varnothing$.

Step 2: 01J3 reduced structure, integral by the equivalence in def-pc-integral-scheme, finite by 035C, proper by closed-immersion-proper (c). Step 3: 0AAX plus irreducibility gives one point. Openness in X comes from the complement being a finite union of the other closed components, using maximality. Step 4: lem-sc-normalization-exists gives finite, surjective, proper and dim 1. Step 5: induction from the empty map (Spec 0) with the binary 0CYI node. Step 6: surjectivity is lifted pointwise; finite ⇒ proper, then composed; empty case from the coproduct union clause. Edge cases tested: X empty, Spec k[ε], a curve plus a non-reduced point, two meeting P¹, a cuspidal curve over an imperfect field.
